title: Post hoc amendment 1: local recalibration of the transported models (RQ3)
status: post hoc: decided after the results of notebook 05 were seen; outside the reading rules of the analysis plan; descriptive

amends.note: The analysis plan is not edited (its hash stays the same); this amendment has its own hash and is frozen by notebook 09 before it runs.

rationale: In RQ3 the frozen models ranked participants well in the other cohort, but their probabilities were miscalibrated (BrainLat -> Greek: calibration slope above 1, risk underestimated; Greek -> BrainLat: risk overestimated). This amendment asks whether a local recalibration, estimated in the target cohort without retraining the model, corrects the probabilities and the decisions at the fixed threshold.

recalibration.intercept_and_slope: logit(p') = a + b * logit(p): logistic recalibration (Cox, 1958; Van Calster et al., 2016)

methods.estimation: logistic regression of the target-cohort diagnoses on logit(p) of the frozen model (MLE; Firth only if the MLE does not converge); logit(p) with p clipped to [0.001, 0.999], as in notebook 05
methods.validation: leave-one-subject-out within the target cohort: the recalibrated probability of each participant uses parameters estimated without that participant
methods.reported_equation: parameters estimated on the whole target cohort (what a new site would apply)
methods.models_retrained: none: the frozen Random Forests of notebook 05 are not changed, so the ranking of the participants (AUC) is that of the frozen models

calibration: calibration-in-the-large (intercept with the slope fixed at 1)
metrics.uncertainty: 95% percentile intervals from 2000 bootstrap resamples of the participants, stratified by diagnosis, with the cross-validated probabilities held fixed (seed 42); the Brier difference uses the same resamples

calibration_curve.interval: Wilson 95% interval of the observed proportion

reporting: Labelled 'post hoc' wherever it appears (Methods, Results, Table S8, Fig. 6). It does not change any reading of RQ1-RQ3.
